The three-stage season ran from February 8 and December 7. [[Sociedad Deportivo Quito|Deportivo Quito]] became the league champion on December 3 by defeating [[Club Social y Deportivo Macará|Macará]] 2–1 in [[Latacunga]].{{cite news|url=https://www.elcomercio.com/deportes/futbol/deportivo-quito-campeon-nacional-saritama/|title=Deportivo Quito 2008, un campeón que llegó 40 años tarde|first=Alexis|last=Sinchire|work=[[El Comercio (Ecuador)|El Comercio]]|date=19 May 2024|access-date=19 June 2025|language=es}} It is Deportivo Quito's 3rd title, and first in 40 years. ==Format== The format for 2008 was new, but similar to the [[2007 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A|2007 Serie A]]. The season was composed of three stages: The format for the '''[[#First stage|First Stage]]''' remained the same. The twelve teams competed against each other in a double [[round-robin tournament|round-robin]] format playing each opponent once at home and once away. The top-four teams at the end of the stage qualified to the Liguilla Final. The top-three teams earned bonus points for the Liguilla Final (3, 2, & 1 point[s] respectively) The top-team of the stage qualified to the last Ecuadorian spot in the [[2008 Copa Sudamericana]]. The format for the '''[[#Second stage|Second Stage]]''' changed. The twelve teams were divided into two groups of six, where they played within their groups in a double round-robin tournament. The winner of the each group qualified to the final two spots in the Liguilla Final. If a team who has already qualified for the Liguilla Final manages to qualify again by winning their group, the last spots for the Liguilla Final went to the highest positioned team(s) in the Aggregate Table who have not already qualified. The top-team of each group received one bonus point for the Liguilla Final (if a team who earned bonus points from the First Stage finishes last in their group, they will lose their bonus points for the Liguilla Final). At the end of this stage, the two teams with the fewest points in the aggregate table were relegated to the [[Serie B de Ecuador|Serie B]] for the 2009 season. The format for the '''[[#Liguilla Final|Liguilla Final]]''' remained the same. The six qualified team competed in a double round-robin tournament. The winner of this stage was crowned the champion of the Copa Pílsener Serie A. The champion will qualified to the [[2009 Copa Libertadores]] Second Stage, while the runner-up and third-place finisher qualify to the First Stage (this slight change from other years is due to the fact that the defending Copa Libertadores champion is an Ecuadorian team). ==Teams== The number of teams for the Serie A expanded this season from 10 to 12. [[Imbabura Sporting Club|Imbabura]] was the only team relegated at the end of the [[2007 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A|2007 season]] by accumulating the fewest points in the [[2007 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A|aggregate table]]. [[Club Deportivo Universidad Católica del Ecuador|Universidad Católica]], [[Club Deportivo ESPOLI|ESPOLI]], and [[Club Deportivo Técnico Universitario|Técnico Universitario]] were promoted as 2007 Serie B winner, runner-up, and third-place finisher, respectively.
